quiz.question: What is the main purpose of following the Rule of Three in code refactoring?

answers.answer: To optimize code performance by using fewer lines of code.
To avoid premature abstraction, which can unnecessarily complicate the code.
To ensure all variables are declared globally for easier access.
To make code abstract right after the first instance of repetition.

quiz.question: When should you consider refactoring according to the Rule of Three?

answers.answer: After identifying the same pattern twice in the code.
As soon as you notice any repetition in the code.
After encountering the same pattern for the third time.
Only during major codebase overhauls mandated by management.

quiz.question: What can happen if you refactor your code too early, according to the Rule of Three?

answers.answer: The code will only become slightly more complex.
There is a risk of unnecessary complications and over-engineering.
All bugs in the code will be automatically resolved.
The code will become non-functional and will not compile.
